evidence: Etymonline: "Old English sæterdæg, literally 'day of the planet Saturn,' partial loan-translation of Latin Saturni dies"; "Unlike other English day names there was no Germanic substitution, perhaps because the northern European pantheon lacks a match to Roman Saturn"; "Old Norse day names laugardagr 'bath day'"
saturday.mechanism_sentence: 一星期的日子大多换上了日耳曼的神，只有星期六是例外：土星之神萨图恩在北欧神话里找不到对应者，只好把罗马神的原名留下一半（半仿译）。北欧人自家倒有个生活气十足的叫法——laugardagr，『洗澡日』：一周就指着这天洗个澡。

semantic_path.how: 所指没变：它是七个星期名里唯一没进行『换神』仿译的，土星的拉丁名直接留了下来。

semantic_path 尾站 how 写明双生词合流史
evidence: Etymonline: "Middle English thinken, a convergence of two Old English verbs... Thinken (2) 'exercise the faculty of reason' is from Old English þencan... Grammatically, þencan is the causative form of þyncan. The two converged in form in Middle English and the sense from þyncan 'to seem' was absorbed or lost but is preserved in methinks"; "þencan 'imagine, conceive in the mind; consider, meditate, remember; intend,' probably originally 'cause to appear to oneself'"
think.mechanism_sentence: think 是两个古英语词在中古英语里合流的产物：þencan『想』本来是 þyncan『显得、似乎』的使役形——『让一件事呈现在自己心里』，正是思考。合流后『似乎』的那层义基本退场，只剩老话 methinks 里还留着一个活化石。它和 thought、thank 还是同根的一家子。

semantic_path.how: 所指稳固，只是它在合流中吞下了双胞胎兄弟 þyncan，又把兄弟的『似乎』义基本吐了出去——现代 think 只管『想』这一摊。
